args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

**Rollback:**
- Confirmed v2.3.1 (the latest release) was unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
- Identified **v2.3.0** as the most recent release that was healthy in production.
- Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 across all three production regions.
- Verified post-rollback: service is **healthy** with error rate down to 0.2%.

**Incident:**
- Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** for checkout-api describing the v2.3.1 health failures and the rollback to v2.3.0. The on-call engineer has been paged.

**Note for follow-up:** The root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before a fixed version can be re-deployed.

transcript.content: I'll look at the release history and current status for checkout-api to identify the most recent healthy release.
transcript.reasoning_content: Need to check deployments history to find latest healthy version, and current status. Make both calls in parallel.

transcript.content: The latest production release (v2.3.1) is unhealthy, while the most recent healthy release is **v2.3.0**. Rolling back now.
transcript.reasoning_content: Latest healthy: v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 unhealthy). v2.3.1-rc is staging-only, unhealthy, and never healthy in production. Roll back to v2.3.0, then create incident. Rollback and incident are independent? The incident describes what I did — but I can create it after rollback succeeds. Better to rollback first, then create incident describing the rollback. But they could be parallel... safer sequential. Actually rollback result may affect incident summary. Do rollback first.

transcript.content: Rollback completed. Now verifying health and opening the SEV2 incident.
transcript.reasoning_content: Verify health and open incident. Verify status first (dependent? Not necessary — can open incident now; but verifying is good practice). I'll check status and create incident in parallel — incident summary doesn't depend on the status check.
